FINDING_ID: IM_F001
SEVERITY: 0.96
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` emits the wrong event type for FORMAT failures. In the FORMAT branch it emits `ManagerEventType.MALFORMED` instead of `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION`. This breaks the immune response boundary because downstream monitoring/event consumers cannot distinguish parse failures from format-compliance failures, so immune logic and operators receive a false diagnosis channel.
PROPOSED_FIX: In the `FORMAT` branch of `detect_failure()`, emit `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION` rather than `ManagerEventType.MALFORMED`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F002
SEVERITY: 0.93
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.88
DESCRIPTION: `process_round()` feeds incorrect failure status into the immune monitor's per-model tracking. It sets `failed = mid not in responses or not responses[mid].parseable`, which only marks missing responses and parse failures as failures. TIMEOUT, EMPTY, FORMAT, and UNDERPERFORM failures detected earlier by `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` are ignored here. As a result, `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_model_round()` undercounts consecutive failures and can miss `model_failure_*` diagnoses or emit them late, distorting the immune layer's own remediation chains.
PROPOSED_FIX: Derive `failed` from the already computed `failures[mid] is not None` or from a stricter subset such as transport/protocol failures, but use the actual detected failure result rather than reparsing `responses`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.86
DESCRIPTION: `process_round()` calls `health_monitor.record_model_round(mid, fc, failed)` without passing `response_time` or `response_chars`, even though `record_model_round()` uses those fields for parser-yield anomaly detection and cost-per-finding spike detection. That makes both immune checks effectively dead in normal integration: `response_chars` stays 0 so parser-yield detection never triggers, and `response_time` stays 0 so CPF-spike detection never triggers.
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass `response_time=responses[mid].response_time` and `response_chars=len(responses[mid].content)` when a response exists, otherwise 0 defaults.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F004
SEVERITY: 0.89
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor.false_positive_rate` claims to be computed over the last 10 rounds, but `total_detections` is counted over all historical diagnoses with no round filter. Only natural resolutions are window-filtered. This biases the denominator upward over time and drives the false-positive rate artificially toward zero, suppressing Level-3 self-diagnosis for over-sensitive detection.
PROPOSED_FIX: Store round metadata for detections and filter both detections and natural resolutions to the same rolling round window before computing the ratio.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F005
SEVERITY: 0.87
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.84
DESCRIPTION: Natural-resolution tracking is internally inconsistent for `mu`. In `record_round()`, resolution records use `record_natural_resolution("mu")` when the pathology count key is `"mu"`, but active remediation for the same issue is keyed as `"mu_distortion"` in `_remediation_state` checks. Because the keys differ, a remediated mu pathology can be misclassified as a natural resolution, inflating false-positive history and corrupting self-diagnosis.
PROPOSED_FIX: Use one canonical pathology key across detection, remediation state, and natural-resolution checks, e.g. always `"mu_distortion"` or always `"mu"`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F006
SEVERITY: 0.85
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_round()` never resets `_pathology_counts["vocab_saturation"]` when the condition clears. Every other persistent pathology has a resolution branch; this one does not. The result is stale persistence state, no natural-resolution logging, and potentially inflated occurrence counts if saturation reappears after recovery.
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an `else` resolution branch mirroring the kappa/findings-decline pattern: increment `_resolved_counts`, optionally call `record_natural_resolution()` when no remediation is active, and reset `_pathology_counts["vocab_saturation"]` to 0.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F007
SEVERITY: 0.82
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.81
DESCRIPTION: `_verify_remediation_outcomes()` uses a generic `current_val > old_val` improvement rule for `vocab_growth`, but the corresponding remediation for `vocab_saturation` lowers `tau_vocab_growth` rather than increasing observed `vocab_growth`. Lowering the threshold may correctly fix false saturation without causing vocab growth itself to rise. This makes the verification criterion mismatched to the intervention, so successful remediations can be marked ineffective and escalated unnecessarily.
PROPOSED_FIX: Verify threshold-based remediations against the pathology predicate they target, e.g. check whether the monitor stops flagging premature vocab saturation, not whether raw `vocab_growth` increased.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F008
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76
DESCRIPTION: The immune feedback loop has no remediation path for several diagnoses it actively emits, including `parser_yield`, `monotonic_decline`, `cpf_spike`, and Level-3 `self_diagnosis` outputs. These diagnoses are logged and replayed as events, but `apply_diagnosis()` returns `None` for them. Given the stated purpose of autonomous remediation chains, this is incomplete integration of the immune layer.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either add explicit remediation chains/handlers for these emitted diagnoses or downgrade/document them as advisory-only so the implementation matches the stated contract.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F009
SEVERITY: 0.78
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_model_round()` and its call site disagree on the meaning of `failed`. The method documentation says "failed/timed out", but internal pathology detection for consecutive model failure is intended to capture broader failure patterns. The integration currently passes a narrow parseability proxy. This interface mismatch makes the immune subsystem fragile and misleading even if the code runs.
PROPOSED_FIX: Define `failed` precisely in the interface contract, preferably as "a FailureHandler-detected failure of configured classes", and pass that exact classification from `process_round()`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F010
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 8
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor.false_positive_rate` docstring says "last 10 rounds", but implementation actually uses all diagnoses ever recorded for the denominator and only windows natural resolutions. This is a documentation/contract bug that obscures a real calibration defect in the immune self-assessment layer.
PROPOSED_FIX: Update implementation to match the documented rolling-window behavior, and if not changed, rewrite the docstring to describe the actual lifetime-denominator calculation.
VERIFIED: TRUE
